title: QFT Zoo standard three-point structures (data/three_point_structures.yaml)
description: The few three-point structures that are standard across the literature, which the values of three-point functions may name by id without defining them in their entry. See docs/THREE_POINT.md.

symbol.description: [latex] The usual symbol for its coefficient.

name.description: [markdown] A short name everyone will understand.

description.description: [markdown] The definition: the three-point function and the normalization of the operators and of the structure.

default.description: The structure a reader assumes when none is named (three scalars, unit-normalized): values in it carry no label on the page; the section says once what unlabelled values mean.

spins.description: Spins of the three operators that the structure is defined for; the build checks them against the operators table.

d.description: The spacetime dimension it is defined in, if only one; the build checks it against the entry.

basis.description: As for an entry's structures: an id shared by the elements of one basis of several independent structures.

relation.description: [markdown] Relations that follow from the definition.

derivation.description: [markdown] Not shown on the page: how the definition follows from the sources, for verifiers.

form.description: [latex] What the structure is, written out or in a form some work has given it; needed unless a single-monomial `embedding` says it. See docs/THREE_POINT.md.

embedding.description: [latex] Optional: the three-point function in embedding space, in the notation of Costa, Penedones, Poland and Rychkov, Spinning Conformal Correlators (arXiv:1107.3554): points P_i, polarizations Z_i, P_{ij} = -2 P_i.P_j, V_{i,jk}, H_{ij}. A formula without $...$, shown in display math. Only for a structure that is a simple embedding-space structure. See docs/THREE_POINT.md.
